answer: Require each agent to post a stake that is locked before it can earn reputation or claim rewards; weight influence by stake and release it only after a long, auditable participation period. If identities coordinate to inflate votes or farm payouts, evidence of collusion triggers slashing, so creating more names does not create free influence. The attacker must tie up real capital, pay setup and operating costs for each identity, and risk losing the stake. A marble, an opal, or an orchard can name an account, but none makes the collateral cost disappear.
